quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You hear a siren while driving but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Drive closer to the car in front of them.
Stay farther away from the car in front of them.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front of them.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, stay farther away from the car in front of you. This gives you more time to stop if needed.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This applies to both controlled and uncontrolled intersections.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright headlights and helps you see enough of the road to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What type of sign has this shape and color?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs like this one are used only to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body get rid of per hour?

options.text: Three drinks an hour.
One drink an hour.
Two drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one alcoholic drink in one hour. How impaired a person becomes depends on many factors, including how much they drank, how fast they drank it, body weight, food intake, and general health.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal to drive?

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving while impaired by alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn now because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When making a left turn with oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass before turning. You may enter the intersection to prepare if the light is green and no other vehicle ahead of you is turning left.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar area. Do not start with only a vague idea of where you are going. Check the location on a map before you drive.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb so your car does not roll into traffic. If there is no curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction the arrow was pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot around a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large vehicle
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is a large blind spot around trucks and other large vehicles. Avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle is more balanced with two riders than with one.
You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane. Make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before passing a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: The driver will turn left.
The driver will turn right.
The driver will stop.
The driver will start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will stop.
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand extended downward means the driver is about to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: When should you leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: On an uphill slope.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an uphill slope.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front when stopped on an uphill slope. This protects you if the vehicle ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing without warning lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Only cross when your entire vehicle fits on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because the vehicle may stall.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is ahead.
You will need to turn left soon.
The road will become narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge marks where the edge is. If the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: If you are convicted of DWI a second time within five years, what will happen?

options.text: You will lose your license for only 90 days.
You will only be able to drive on residential roads.
You must install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID).
You must drive 10 mph slower than the speed limit at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID).
questions.explanation: A second DWI conviction within five years has serious consequences. Your license may be suspended for one year or denied for five years. You may also face a $1,000 fine and/or up to one year in jail. Before you can drive again, you must install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID).

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph needs about ____ feet to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks take much longer to stop than regular cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs almost 400 feet to stop completely when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading straight at you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer to the right to escape. Do not steer left—the other driver may correct at the last second and you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Losing speed reduces the impact of a collision.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow on a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow is pointing to.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in the direction of the arrow. However, oncoming traffic has a green light. You must yield to all oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to the lane you were just in.
Either lane is fine.
It does not matter which lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you were just in.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from. This is the safest way to turn.
